project: kcl/tawk — TAwk : TUtil, GNU Awk wrapper (5.0.0 under bash 5.2.37, 5.4.0 under 5.3.9): program + addProgram + programFile, verbatim setVar (-v with an encoding), sandbox on by default and fail-closed, in-place with run only, static one-liner TAwk.apply.
status: P0 DONE 2026-09-23 (commit 2472b04): tawk.sh + tests 004/005/006 (580 checks) green on bash 5.2.37 / gawk 5.0.0 and bash 5.3.9 / gawk 5.4.0; README first cut; tutil PLAN §7 + docs §4 tawk rows. P1 (closeout) planned. Planned and critic-hardened 2026-09-23 (20 findings, record in PLAN §8).

decisions.Q1: sandbox = 1 by default, fail-closed (only the exact string 0 drops --sandbox), as TSed
decisions.Q2: setVar NAME VALUE is verbatim, implemented as -v NAME=enc(VALUE) (every backslash doubled, newline as \n, a leading @ as \100) — measured byte-exact on both gawk versions; the first draft's env + ENVIRON prologue was dropped (its premise came from a probe corrupted by the Bash tool collapsing backslashes; it also cost +13-25 ms per run)
decisions.Q3: as TSed: program + addProgram/clearPrograms + programFile; rc 1/2 -> 1 + debug, any other (exit N) -> 1 silent; a deny-list for addArg
decisions.Q4: as TSed: inPlace + backupSuffix (inplace::suffix), run only, the five sinks overridden, inPlace derives BINMODE=3; inPlace requires sandbox = 0 (the sandbox refuses the inplace extension); the include is loaded by absolute path /usr/share/awk/inplace.awk (AWKPATH starts with . — a planted ./inplace.awk would run)

execution_log.summary: Worker (Opus). Red first: 004/005/006 written against a stubbed skeleton, 549 FAIL of 572 on bash 5.2.37 (004 384/390, 005 101/103, 006 64/79). Then tawk.sh per PLAN §1.2: Create (parent.constructor gawk, nine vars, sandbox=1, indexed _paths/_progs/_vnames/_vvals), Destroy, paths, addProgram/clearPrograms, setVar (identifier + keyword/builtin/array check, in-place replacement)/clearVars, buildArgv (pinned argv; empty chunks never emitted; the §2.2 rc 2 list incl. assignment-looking paths, inPlace needing sandbox 0, and the getopt-following deny-list: any prefix of a denied long name, -W attached/separate/abbreviated/bundled, bundles, --, non-option words, dangling -v/--assign/-W, -P/-c while BINMODE is derived; -v NAME=enc(VALUE) after the extras; the absolute inplace include), mapRc (Q3), the five sinks (inPlace -> rc 2, else the rc-preserving spelling), static apply ('' and no path rc 2, sandbox forced). Green: 572/572 on 5.2.37 (threaded and --mode single) and 5.3.9; tutil/tgrep/thead/ttail/tfind/tsed unchanged on 5.2.37. README first cut; tutil PLAN §7 and docs §4 tawk rows. Probes run with stdin closed under timeout; gawk 5.4 probed only under msys64's own bash (launching it from Git's bash crosses msys runtimes and mangles `{...}` and '' arguments). Tool trap found: the Write tool decodes a literal backslash-u escape, so the backslash-u0041 value is built at run time in 005. REVIEW (supervisor, 2026-09-24): suite reproduced 580/580 on bash 5.2.37 (gawk 5.0.0) and 5.3.9 (gawk 5.4.0), no gawk process left; review question 6 answered YES — backupSuffix now goes through the same enc as setVar (6 red of 8 new cases before the fix). Master sweep: 5.2.37 28/28 0 [FAIL]; 5.3.9 first run failed two load-sensitive timing assertions in untouched units (tinifile 011_T6 position ratio, tstringlist 013 Assign vs Adds) with no runaway process on the machine (sampled per-process CPU), the rerun 28/28 0 [FAIL] — open item: loosen those two ceilings. Committed as kcl 2472b04.

Opus critic, prototype on the real tutil, both gawk versions (5.0.0 / 5.4.0), every probe with stdin closed. BLOCKER: -e '' is dropped by gawk and the first path becomes the program (a path named 1 hung reading stdin) -> empty chunks never emitted, no-program rc 2, apply '' rc 2. MAJORS: -W long-option spelling bypassed the deny-list and a dangling -W swallowed the generated prologue; a non-option extra becomes THE program; -o -g -h -V -C -d -p -D skip the program, write files under the sandbox, print to stdout or hang; 5.4 + sandbox + -M loses the input; -i inplace resolves through AWKPATH (. first) so a planted ./inplace.awk ran with the sandbox off -> absolute include path; a missing input file is FATAL (later files never read or edited); and -v with doubled backslashes DOES round-trip — the supervisor re-checked through a file and confirmed it (the planning probe had been corrupted by the Bash tool collapsing backslashes in an inline command), with one extra rule found in the re-check: newline as \n. The env + prologue design was dropped. MINOR/NIT: indexed var storage (hash order), keyword/builtin names refused, namespaced assignment operands, a fuller sandbox list, in-place traps (exit truncates, END to stdout, ENDFILE into the file), BINMODE disabled by --posix/-c, programFile via AWKPATH and -f -, version-dependent abbreviations (refuse any prefix), chunks cannot span -e words, callback trap, the directory warning identical on both.

Owner: push, then tawk. Two gawk versions measured (5.0.0 under bash 5.2.37 via Git for Windows, 5.4.0 under 5.3.9 via msys64), behaviour identical except messages and INPLACE_SUFFIX. Facts: -e/-f concatenate in argument order; no program -> the first operand is the program and stdin may be read (the planning probe HUNG on `gawk '{print FILENAME}' k=v` — an assignment operand, not a file); rc 1 syntax/fatal, 2 missing input (partial) / missing -f / sandbox fatal, exit N mod 256, a directory is skipped with a warning (rc 0); -v processes escapes and backslash doubling does not round-trip, ENVIRON is verbatim; text mode strips CR, BINMODE=3 keeps it; RS NUL needs ORS NUL for NUL output; print terminates an unterminated last line; --sandbox refuses system/redirection/pipes AND extensions, so -i inplace needs sandbox off; inplace::suffix works on both versions. Owner decided: sandbox as sed (on, fail-closed); setVar verbatim; model and rc as sed; in-place as sed. PLAN.md + this ledger written. No code.
